dramatic_truth: Greg's first trial shell makes him worse at walking on purpose so Masta can see the uncorrected body map she actually has to fit.
performance: He stops hiding mistakes, reports pressure honestly, accepts one second of hands-free standing as data rather than transformation, and leaves the shell at the shop.
screenplay: Full recovery workday; after-work fitting; initial rail steps fail; Masta adjusts socket and rotation; brief hands-free stand; session stops before Greg wants; crutches remain faster and primary.
prose_comparison: The repeated bad steps are fitting evidence and emotional payoff without montage shortcuts.

dramatic_truth: A no-shell recovery day teaches Greg that temporary work, fittings, home communication, and belonging can coexist without every day maximizing income.
performance: He accepts flex employment, treats crutches as excellent current mobility rather than obsolete gear, receives Carrow's delayed reply, and gives Duskport a bounded several-more-days horizon.
screenplay: Post-fitting soreness; Venn flex-work terms; Masta confirms no shell; Carrow letter from Cala/Tavi/Lyssa arrives; Greg replies with current plans and trial-shell status.
prose_comparison: The quieter day integrates distance, home, work optionality, and fitting recovery rather than repeating logistics.

dramatic_truth: Greg deliberately declines available work before his second shell session, proving rest can be an active fitting choice rather than lost earnings.
performance: He checks boring skin, refuses to convert the free day into labor exchange or magic training, then lets Masta compare rested volume and build better data.
screenplay: Morning no-work decision; ordinary errands; second fitting; repeated honest bad turns; hands-free standing grows from seconds rather than breakthrough; shell remains shop-owned.
prose_comparison: The chapter's repetition differentiates rested-body data from after-work data and advances both discipline and fit.

dramatic_truth: A third shell session after a real workday tests whether the fit can function on Greg's actual tired, slightly swollen body rather than an ideal fitting-room version.
performance: He self-seats and self-corrects the shell, moves from rails into courtyard, carries a five-pound box three ugly steps with crutches bundled in one hand, and stops before proving anything beyond the test.
screenplay: Venn workday; after-work volume check; revised foot/strap setup; rail walking; courtyard drain and light-crutch trials; three loaded steps; skin remains useful rather than damaged.
prose_comparison: Repeated fitting work changes the variable from rested to worked body and produces the first movement with hands occupied by tasks instead of support.

dramatic_truth: Greg's first one-hour city trial changes the question from whether the limb can replace crutches to what new functions it adds to his world map.
performance: He keeps crutches with him, obeys flat-route limits, stops and resets when patterns degrade, and notices concrete new possibilities like handling bread or standing at counters with freer hands.
screenplay: Shop-to-fountain-market loop; threshold, curb, crowd and Glass Lane problems become measured route data; skin remains within limits; Greg reframes progress as newly nonzero options rather than restored old body.
prose_comparison: The route detail is the payoff because every ordinary obstacle acquires a new movement grammar.

dramatic_truth: On a shell-recovery day Greg finds a northbound Greyfin Road contract that fits his existing field skills and discovers the fitting process can travel with him without becoming the reason for the trip.
performance: He asks terrain, boarding, contract, return, load, survey authority, and departure-window questions before committing; Masta allows a possible second-relay road test only under strict separation of trip value and limb value.
screenplay: Venn has no work; Tavren passes Outer Works notice; Enna Ro interviews Greg for settlement dispute; second relay protects fitting appointment; companions independently want to travel too.
prose_comparison: The chapter expands geographic optionality while preserving the distinction between job, fitting, companions, and curiosity.

dramatic_truth: Masta clears Greg's medium-foot trial build for tightly bounded road use, and the Greyfin contract becomes a real chosen departure rather than a prosthetic field test disguised as adventure.
performance: Greg accepts written wear limits, packs the shell rather than wearing it by default, records whether it is worn as a possible observation variable, and tells home he is moving again without disappearing.
screenplay: Medium-foot shop/courtyard check; redness clears in twenty minutes; Masta releases trial build with strict road rules; Outer Works briefing frames benchmark dispute; companions prepare for second relay; letter sent to Carrow.
prose_comparison: The rules are not bureaucratic filler; they are what keep travel, work, and body experimentation from contaminating one another.

dramatic_truth: Greyfin Section One turns the road dispute into live evidence where a moved benchmark and a moving road can both be true.
performance: Greg preserves observation roles, uses the named boarding accommodation without pride theater, leaves the shell packed until useful, and records wheel response and tactile crutch vibration separately from survey measurements.
screenplay: Pre-dawn relay; South Approach controls; light and heavier cart passes; benchmark/reference disagreement begins shrinking; Greg earns master-ledger responsibility.
prose_comparison: Road-pass repetition is the controlled comparison needed to keep 'benchmark moved' from becoming 'road fine.'

dramatic_truth: At Section Three, a class-eight monitored pass visibly extends a road crack, forcing carrier economics, village fuel needs, and engineering caution into one constrained decision.
performance: Greg records sound, wheel position and crack growth without assigning cause; Halen and Enna keep claims narrow; Jorren and Tera negotiate clinic-fuel transfer rather than pretending the whole freight problem is solved.
screenplay: B-seven proven moved; rock controls still support road lowering; class-eight test produces grind and crack extension; heavy hold remains; class-six local passage retained; clinic drums get a partial workaround.
prose_comparison: The argument and measurement sequence is decision evidence. It is not repeated road bureaucracy.

dramatic_truth: Rain-day crib inspection reveals both road settlement and blocked drainage/rot, allowing temporary class-seven fuel passage after repair without declaring the causeway fixed.
performance: Greg keeps the trial limb unused on unstable wet work, records slips and tool events without unnecessary names, and distinguishes temporary operational permission from structural resolution.
screenplay: Section Three shoulder opened; rot and drainage problem exposed; crib repair and class-seven test; two transferred fuel loads cross before hard-rain suspension; depot reserve improves to 2.4 days; Greg declines optional evening shell wear due fatigue.
prose_comparison: The chapter demonstrates multiple simultaneous truths and time-buying infrastructure decisions. Hidden status does not make the episodic state expendable.
